[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Thomas Glasgow was born about 1766 and died in 1851. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Mill-357|Janet Mill]].<ref>FamilySearch. https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RG-JFP (accessed 2025).</ref><ref>BillionGraves. https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 (accessed 2025).</ref>
== Research Notes ==
=== Parish household review, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1451|Catharine Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]]: 71% → 97% (confident). Livingston OPR 669/1 item 4 names Catharine, born 20 August and baptised 31 August 1780 at Blackburne, father Thos Glasgow and mother Christian Davidson. Exact dates, full parental couple and locality identify Thomas-1382’s adult family; the same Thomas/Christine Davidson household is separately recorded for Peter in 1790. The literal parents resolve the earlier limitation of the unquoted FamilySearch citation. 97% concerns the Thomas/Christian Davidson adult household, not the adult’s identification as the 1746 Davistoun child. The inherited circa-1766 birth claim conflicts with fatherhood in 1774 and remains unresolved alongside the preferred earlier baptism attribution; no vital date is silently changed. Two indexes describe one baptism. No trade is supplied here; original register image uninspected.

[[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]]: 98% → 78% (probable). Livingston’s 2 February 1746 Davistoun baptism names Thomas Glasgow and Janet Mill; that recorded-child father clause retains 98% conditional confidence. The same Livingston setting and feasible ages for the Christian Davidson adult’s 1774–1790 children support the identification. A retained circa-1766 birth claim conflicts with fatherhood in 1774 and is not resolved by Catharine’s new parent fields. Without a direct childhood-to-adult bridge, assess the complete adult-to-Thomas-1023 placement at 78%. The displayed percentage now covers the adult household’s ancestry. Preserve the former 98% as the conditional 1746 child assessment, not as disproved evidence. The inherited 1766/1851 lifetime may be erroneous or another man; retain that discrepancy without silently changing vitals or certifying the identity. Catharine’s 97% adult-household father link is separate. Original register images uninspected.

Earlier dated percentages and interpretations below are retained as superseded history for these pairs; the current assessments and their specific identity limits are stated here. No live WikiTree changes have been made by this local review.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1023]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Thomas’s 1746 Livingston transcript names Thomas Glasgow and Janet Mill at Davistoun. The existing Thomas-1023 account is the maintained father with Janet Mill and the matching family sequence. Janet Kilpatrick is his mother, not a competing spouse.

Recorded 1746 child and Thomas/Janet Mill household98%; this does not prove every later Thomas identity or the father’s own Kilwinning childhood. Original uninspected.

Next useful test: Keep the later adult Thomas identity separate while checking the original 1746 entry.
